choices.text: Not bad at all! It's giving me a few ideas.

response.speaker: Wislawa
response.text: Hmph, Edler's not the brightest, but she's done a good job with this fun little distraction...

response.speaker: Wislawa
response.text: Haha, anything I tell you, I'm more than happy to say to her face. Besides, I'm only speaking the truth!

response.speaker: Wislawa
response.text: She seems to think I don't know who she is, but when she stopped me in Fontaine, I knew immediately what her deal was — there was a Maison Gardiennage mark on her weapon...

response.speaker: Wislawa
response.text: But it seems to me that it's more fun to watch her keep merrily playing the part of a "kind-hearted merchant."

response.speaker: Wislawa
response.text: A righteous Fontainian plainclothes detective stuck in a place like this, having to convince a "kind-hearted bodyguard" not to call the authorities, completely unable to reveal her identity...

response.speaker: Wislawa
response.text: It's like the plot of some farcical film!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That sounds like something I might watch...

response.speaker: Wislawa
response.text: Truth be told, I just wanted to spar with her — she keeps overthinking the whole thing.

response.speaker: Wislawa
response.text: Alright, that's enough talking, you go ahead and have fun! This wargame has a lot to unpack.

choices.text: This is the first time we've met...
Actually, I'm more interested in your background.

response.speaker: Wislawa
response.text: Me? I'm not like you — a big fish who the Harbingers treat like an honored guest — I'm just small fry, one of their minions. I'm barely worth mentioning.

response.speaker: Wislawa
response.text: But I can tell you something. Even though a minnow like me doesn't usually hear much, I had a boss who used to love yabbering back in the day.

response.speaker: Wislawa
response.text: #That's how I heard of the legendary {NICKNAME}, an exceptional fighter with a brain to match!

response.speaker: Wislawa
response.text: I remember thinking at the time, if we ever met in battle, how little time would it take before you turned me into a ghost?

response.speaker: Wislawa
response.text: *sigh* It doesn't help to think too far ahead. You should get back to your game.

choices.text: I'm more curious about your holiday...

response.speaker: Wislawa
response.text: *sigh* When I was still just a little sprat, I only had about... maybe 10 days a year where I could float up to the shallows and swim freely in the sunlight.

response.speaker: Wislawa
response.text: Well, now that I've a little more weight to throw around, I get a few more days off.

response.speaker: Wislawa
response.text: One day, if I can grow into a shark, I'll command the best treatment there is — 25 days of annual leave!

response.speaker: Wislawa
response.text: When that day comes, I'll make sure to find the warmest waters to really kick back and unwind...

response.speaker: Wislawa
response.text: Better get a move on then — the wargame's just over there.

dialogues.speaker: Wislawa
dialogues.text: *sigh* I'm almost out of holiday. Who knows when we'll meet again...

choices.text: Might as well take the opportunity to play another wargame.

response.speaker: Wislawa
response.text: Ha, you're right, why not focus on having a little fun while I'm still off duty?

choices.text: How about you try sparring with me?

response.speaker: Wislawa
response.text: Haha, take it easy. I'd prefer not to throw hands with you unless it was utterly unavoidable.

response.speaker: Wislawa
response.text: I'd much prefer to find out once and for all who's stronger, me or Edler. She's a fitting opponent — a contest is only fun when both sides are evenly matched, am I right?

choices.text: I look forward to seeing you the next time you're off duty.

response.speaker: Wislawa
response.text: Me too... If only I had a little more holiday to take.

response.speaker: Wislawa
response.text: Then maybe I could be like you, traveling around without a care in the world...
